base_case: Over the next 30-60 days the base case is continued churn-to-melt-up toward the Wave 1 valuation ceiling near 7,695 (Monte Carlo upside target), with the rally visibly decelerating into all-time highs. Probabilistically the upside target is hit first ~63% of the time, but with ERP at zero, breadth divergent, and credit in extreme fear, the risk-reward favors trimming into strength rather than adding, with a 5-8% pullback toward the 38.2% fib / liquidation-nervous zone a live secondary scenario.

valuation_bucket: Forward PE 21.47x (cautious buying only at strong confluence, trim bias rising); ERP +0.18% sits in the 0.0-0.5% valuation-ceiling band — trim bias, no aggressive adds.

Fifth consecutive ATH close but smallest gain of the streak (+0.26%), signaling rally deceleration.

narrative_summary: SPX printed its fifth consecutive all-time-high close at 7,599.96 but the smallest gain of the streak (+0.26%) on a weak middle-third close, signaling a rally running out of buyers rather than building a base. Structure is Late Bull / Topping: trend is intact and Monte Carlo still favors the upside target first (~63%), but every confirming layer is at a cycle extreme — ERP at zero for seven sessions, junk-bond demand in extreme fear, breadth divergent, VIX at complacent lows, and put/call near cycle complacency. The strongest confirming signal is the still-bullish trend regime and melt-up probability edge; the biggest unresolved risk is the simultaneous credit-and-breadth divergence beneath new highs. Posture for next session is hold and monitor — trim into the 7,695 valuation ceiling, no new adds, and prepare staged re-entry at the 38.2% fib / liquidation zones on any pullback.

Fifth consecutive ATH close confirms melt-up momentum has outperformed the topping thesis so far.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Price at new ATHs with intact uptrend justifies holding equities.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: ERP at +0.18% (zero band) for a 7th session means equities offer essentially no premium over risk-free — a valuation ceiling demanding trim bias, not adds.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: ERP in 0.0-0.5% band = valuation ceiling, trim bias, no aggressive adds.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: New ATH closes suggest demand remains in control.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Breadth (McClellan, stock price strength) and credit (junk extreme fear) both diverge from price for 7 sessions — narrow leadership beneath the index.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not broken down.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: VIX ~15 and put/call ~0.60 reflect calm, orderly conditions supporting the trend.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Maximum complacency (VIX cycle low, put/call near cycle low) alongside F&G falling 3 straight sessions at new highs is a classic topping warning — falling sentiment near new highs.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Falling sentiment during or near new highs is a topping warning; deep complacency in put/call is a trim warning.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Monte Carlo upside-first probability ~63% favors the melt-up to 7,695.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: 63% adjusted probability falls below the 70% Late Bull / Topping threshold, so the setup is not actionable as an add even though it favors holders.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Never use Monte Carlo in isolation; if adjusted prob is below the regime threshold the setup is not actionable.

primary_tension: An intact, still-rising bull trend with a Monte Carlo upside edge is colliding with cycle-extreme exhaustion signals — ERP at zero, credit and breadth divergence beneath new highs, peak complacency, and a decelerating, distribution-style close — leaving the market in a hold-and-trim posture rather than an add posture.
